In view of the above, the respondents are directed to release the seized goods involved herein retaining a small quantity of the same for the purpose of sample analysis, if need be, provided the petitioner furnished security in the sum of Rs.7,00,000/- (Rupees:
Seven Lacs).
Further, the petitioner would include in the label the required warning "Not for human consumption" in the large font size (min. 20 pt.).
Matter be listed in the second week of July, 2019.

In the meanwhile,
State-respondents may file their counter- affidavit, if so advised.

For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Ravi Kasliwal For Respondent(s) : Mr. Manish Kumar Sharma for Mr. Rajesh Mahrshi, AAG HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VEERENDR SINGH SIRADHANA Order 27/05/2019
At the motion stage on 21st May, 2019, while issuing the notices to the respondents, this Court did not make any interim order intending to first have the response of the State- respondents.
Mr. Maniesh Kumar Sharma, Assistant to Mr. Rajesh Maharshi, AAG, is not in a position to resist the prayer of the petitioner for grant of interim relief for want of necessary instructions.
(2 of 2) [CW-8993/2019
] Learned counsel for the petitioner, referring to the opinion of the High Court of Madras (Madurai Bench), in the case of R. Chandramohan Versus The Food Safety Officer Vikaramasingapuram & Ors.: Writ Petition (MD) Number 19499 of 2014, decided on 22nd July,
2016, contended that if the label of a product clearly mentions that the oil contained in it is not for edible use, then it is not covered under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short "Act of 2006"), at all.
Learned counsel for the State-respondents could not point out as to how the goods seized with the label specifically indicating "not for edible consumption"; the article would be within the definition of "Food" as defined under the Act of 2006 and Rules framed thereunder.
